Two tankers attacked off Saudi Arabia, one by RPG fired from small boat, UKMTO says
Two tankers were attacked northeast of Al Jubayl, Saudi Arabia, on Friday, the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations (UKMTO) said on Saturday.
Iran’s Intelligence Ministry said on Saturday that 11 people had been arrested in the western Ilam province, in connection with January protests.
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi said on Saturday that Egypt was prepared to take any measures necessary to defend Saudi Arabia, following attacks on the kingdom by Yemen's Iran Houthis.
Iran has helped the Houthis target drone and missile attacks and provided training, intelligence and tactical guidance for attacks on Saudi Arabia and its Yemeni allies, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people briefed on intelligence from Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s anti-Houthi alliance.
Trump said earlier Friday that the US may strike Iran’s fortified Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site “very soon,” while reiterating that Tehran would not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon.

'War booty' iPhones hit Tehran market, police warn of scams
Apple's iPhone 18 smartphones are being advertised in Tehran at unusually low prices as "war booty," supposedly recovered from a cargo ship sunk near the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian media reported Saturday.
The advertisements followed the reported sinking of a container ship near the strait on October 13. Videos circulated on social media purportedly showing iPhones and expensive perfumes floating in the water as people collected them.
Iran's cyber police warned buyers against paying deposits or advance fees before inspecting the goods and verifying sellers' identities. Officials warned that scammers could exploit the shipwreck story to advertise nonexistent products at attractive prices.

Sisi seeks parliament's approval, calls Saudi defense imperative
Sisi called for an emergency parliamentary session to authorize possible action, while Egypt's parliament announced it would convene on the matter Sunday, Reuters reported.
"It is inconceivable that we would allow Saudi Arabia, its security or stability to be harmed," Sisi said at a military academy ceremony.

Iran vice president calls for urgent shift away from southern ports
Iran must urgently reduce its reliance on southern ports and develop alternative trade routes to overcome wartime maritime restrictions, the country's vice president for parliamentary and strategic affairs said on Saturday.
Speaking at a meeting with government officials and business representatives, Mohsen Esmaeili said diversifying trade routes would make Iran more resilient and should remain a long-term priority beyond the current war.

Egypt, Turkey urge renewed US-Iran talks to end crisis
The foreign ministers of Egypt and Turkey called for renewed negotiations between the United States and Iran, describing diplomacy as the only way to end the current crisis and prevent further escalation, Egypt's State Information Service reported Saturday.
Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty and his Turkish counterpart Hakan Fidan met on the sidelines of an Organization of Islamic Cooperation foreign ministers' meeting in Baghdad, where they discussed regional developments, including Iran, and efforts to reduce tensions.

A new message issued in the name of Iran's Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei appeared on his X account on Saturday, congratulating the country's under-23 Greco-Roman wrestling team on winning the world championship in the United States.
Oct 17, 2026, 15:04 GMT+1
Iranian political prisoner begins dry hunger strike over denied medical care
Political prisoner Kazem Alinejad has begun a dry hunger strike at Tehran's Evin Prison to protest being denied essential medication and medical treatment, a source familiar with his case told Iran International.
The source said Alinejad suffers from heart and kidney problems, but prison authorities have refused to provide his medication or transfer him to a hospital. Sores on his legs have also left him unable to walk.
Alinejad intends to continue refusing food until his medical needs are addressed, the source said, warning that his deteriorating situation could put his life at serious risk.
Alinejad was sentenced to 11 years in prison by Tehran's Revolutionary Court in January 2024. An appeals court later reduced his sentence to six years, with five years to be served.
Oct 17, 2026, 14:23 GMT+1
LNG tanker reports shots fired by skiff off Yemen - UKMTO
The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations said Saturday it received a report of an incident involving an LNG tanker 140 nautical miles southeast of Yemen’s Al Mukalla.
The tanker’s master reported being approached by a small skiff carrying seven people, which fired two shots at the vessel, UKMTO said. The tanker’s armed security team fired two warning shots, forcing the skiff to alter course.
Authorities are investigating the incident, UKMTO added.
Oct 17, 2026, 13:52 GMT+1
Iran says it sent Washington Hormuz reopening plan via mediator Qatar
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said Saturday Tehran had sent Washington, through mediator Qatar, a seven-day plan under which the Strait of Hormuz could reopen and normal maritime traffic resume if the Islamic Republic’s conditions were met.
“We conveyed a specific seven-day plan and said that if the necessary conditions are met, the Strait can be reopened and normal maritime traffic can resume within seven days,” Araghchi said. “The choice is now America’s.”
Araghchi said US military actions had prevented implementation of the June memorandum of understanding and that dispute-resolution mechanisms envisaged under the agreement had been ignored.
“You cannot bomb a country, threaten to destroy it and blockade it, and then expect maritime security to return to normal,” he said.
“The Islamic Republic does not accept coercion, threats or intimidation and will not relinquish its sovereign rights under pressure,” he said. “But it remains ready for dialogue based on mutual respect and credible guarantees.”
On the war between Yemen’s Houthis and Saudi Arabia, Araghchi said Tehran supported the sovereignty and territorial integrity of both countries and was ready to help facilitate dialogue based on a previously agreed peace roadmap.
Oct 17, 2026, 13:17 GMT+1
IRGC Navy claims second supertanker hit naval mine in Strait of Hormuz
The IRGC Navy claimed Saturday that a second supertanker struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz and caught fire, alleging the vessel was carrying more than two million barrels of crude oil and trying to pass through what it called an “illegal” route.
The force said the tanker had switched off all positioning and radar systems and alleged it had done so “with deception” by the US military.
According to the IRGC Navy, the mine strike caused a powerful explosion in the vessel’s engine room and left the tanker stopped at the site.

Yemen army says Houthis suffered casualties and equipment losses in Marib
Yemen’s armed forces said on Saturday that Houthi forces had suffered casualties and lost military equipment in Marib.
